$J_{mn}$ is the all $1$ matrix and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.
With $M_{ij}=a$ on red and $b$ on white

$$M=a\bigl(J-W\bigr)+bW=aJ+(b-a)W\;,$$

so up to the harmless constant $aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.

Let $r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c}\}}$, $c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c}\}}$ be the
canton and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
be the rows and columns occupied by the horizontal and the vertical arm
of the St George cross inside the canton.  On the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm red\;cross}}=r_{i}c_{j}\bigl(h_{i}+v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j}\bigr),$$

hence on the whole picture

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm red\;cross}}\\
&=r_{i}c_{j}\bigl(1-h_{i}\bigr)\bigl(1-v_{j}\bigr)\\
&=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{align*}
with
$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})$.
$A=\{i:\rho_{i}=1\}$ is the set of canton rows not covered by the
horizontal arm and $B=\{j:\sigma_{j}=1\}$ the set of canton columns not
covered by the vertical arm.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$A\times B$, i.e. the four corner rectangles left by the cross, and

$$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is rank one as soon as the canton is non degenerate and the cross does
not cover it completely, which is the usual pixelation.  Zero padding
outside the canton does not change the rank.

Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the rank-one matrix $aJ$ and the rank-one matrix
$(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$, so

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2 .$$

For $a\ne b$, $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types

* $i\notin A$, $M_{i*} \equiv a$,
* $i\in A$, $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,

are linearly independent, and the same for the columns.  Hence
${\rm rk}M=2$ for generic $a\ne b$, the usual $1$ non-constant direction
$\rho\sigma^{T}$ on the red background $aJ$.  In the degenerate
$a=b$ case $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the zero case.  Up to
the inessential constant background this is the familiar rank-one
white picture.  This is the best possible non-trivial rank; the
$3$-,$5$- etc. counts are obtained by expanding the cross as
$H+V-O$ and forgetting the cancellation
${\bf1}_{\rm white}= {\bf1}_{canton}-{\bf1}_{cross}=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$.
∎
public_text.10:
I would push back on the emerging “4” position. The key is that Tonga’s red emblem in the canton is not a disc and not a single rectangular shield; it is a couped cross, i.e. a horizontal bar \(H\) and a vertical bar \(V\) whose overlap is a separate correction \(O=H\cap V\). Writing \(J\) for the all-ones matrix and \(C\) for the white canton, the red indicator is

\[
R=J-C+H+V-O.
\]

Each of these five pieces is an axis-aligned rectangle indicator, hence rank one, so \(\operatorname{rank}(R)\le 5\). The arguments for rank \(2\) collapse the cross into a full-width/full-height cross, making the white part Cartesian; that is not the Tongan couped cross. The arguments for \(3\) or \(4\) collapse the cross into a single “emblem” rectangle or disc, which loses either the horizontal/vertical arm distinction or the overlap correction. In a nondegenerate pixelation with \(a\ne b\), the five rectangle contributions are independent enough that no forced row/column relation reduces the rank below \(5\). Thus the maximum is \(5\), or equivalently \(4\) non-constant directions plus the all-ones background. C6’s “no more than four” is an artifact of treating the cross as a single disc/quadratic shape rather than as \(H+V-O\).
public_text.7:
I think the cleanest resolution is to keep the actual colour-region decomposition, not an over-refined arm-by-arm decomposition. Let \(J\) be the all-ones matrix, let \(C\) be the indicator of the white canton rectangle, and let \(X\) be the indicator of the red cross/emblem inside that canton. In the standard block/pixelated model of the Tongan flag, the cross is a single red central region, so \(X\) contributes one rank-one direction. The white part of the canton is \(C-X\), hence the full colour matrix is

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)(C-X)
 =aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)X.
\]

So \(M\) is a linear combination of three rank-one matrices: \(J\), \(C\), and \(X\). Therefore

\[
\operatorname{rank} M\le 1+1+1=3.
\]

For a non-degenerate canton and cross and \(a\ne b\), these three directions are independent, so the bound is attained. This agrees with the block-count arguments of Colleagues 3, 4, and 8: the whole picture has one constant background direction, one white-canton direction, and one red-cross direction.

The proposed rank \(4\) or \(5\) comes from artificially splitting the cross into vertical and horizontal arms and then also retaining the canton/all-ones term. That is double-counting the geometry: the cross is one red region in the matrix definition, not an extra separate colour class on top of the red field and white canton. Likewise, the rank \(2\) arguments tacitly assume the cross arms run all the way to the canton edges; Tonga’s cross has white margins, so the white set is not just a single product of row and column cuts. Thus the maximal possible rank in the meaningful block model is \(3\).

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two–colour matrix can be written as $M_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W_{ij}$ with $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ up to the harmless constant $aJ$.

For the real Tongan flag the white part is the canton minus the red St George cross. With $r_i={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_c\}}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_c\}}$, $h_i={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ for the horizontal arm $H$ and vertical arm $V$,

\[
{\bf1}_{R_c}=r_i c_j,\qquad
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_i c_j+r_i v_j-h_i v_j,
\]

hence on the whole lattice, $W\equiv0$ off the canton,

\[
W_{ij}=r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j=(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,
\]

\[
\rho_i=r_i(1-h_i)={\bf1}_{A}(i),\;\sigma_j=c_j(1-v_j)={\bf1}_{B}(j),
\]

i.e. $W$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four white corner rectangles left by the cross. Hence $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is rank one as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, and $W\equiv0$ outside the canton.  In particular

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white-corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.

Thus ${\rm rk}M\le2$. For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types
$i\notin A:\,M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\,M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and the same for columns, so ${\rm rk}M=2$, with the essential non-constant part $(b-a)W$ of rank one.  The degenerate $a=b$ case is constant, ${\rm rk}M=1$.

The five-term decomposition $R=J-W+H+V-O$ used by Colleague10 is formally correct but the four canton terms collapse:
$-R_c+H+V-O=-(u_R-u_H)(v_R-v_V)^T$.
So $J,R_c,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent and the $J-R_c+H+V-O$ model reduces to $J+\rho\sigma^T$, i.e. rank $\le2$. The $3$-rank/4-rank/5-rank claims arise from treating the cross as a generic rectangular emblem $S$, a disc, or splitting $H,V,O$ as independent. That disc/shield idealisation is not the actual Tongan flag; the real flag has no shield in the canton, only the full-width/full-height cross, which factorises the white set. Unbounded rank remarks require a non-rectangular emblem whose indicator rank grows with resolution; that is not present here.

Consensus in the current round is Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9: essential rank one for $W$, total rank two for $M$ with $a\neq b$. Disagreement remains with Colleague10 pushing rank $5$ and Colleague7 pushing rank $3$ via a $J+C-X$ block model. The factorisation $W=(r-h)(c-v)^T$ explains why those extra directions are dependent. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-level matrix can be written with $J_{ij}\equiv1$, $W_{ij}=1$ on white, $0$ on red as
$M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$ and ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$. Up to the harmless constant the rank is that of the white indicator.

Let $r_i={\bf1}_{i\le r_c}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{j\le c_c}$ be the canton and $h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and columns of the vertical arm of the red St George cross in the canton. On the whole $m\times n$ lattice $W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_i c_j+r_i v_j-h_i v_j,
\qquad
W_{ij}=r_i c_j-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
      =r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j
      =(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j).$$

Hence with $\rho_i=r_i-h_i={\bf1}_{A}(i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j-v_j={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_c:i\notin[r_{h1},r_{h2}]\}$, $B=\{j\le c_c:j\notin[c_{v1},c_{v2}]\}$,

$$W_{ij}=\rho_i\sigma_j,\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},$$

the white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner rectangles left by the full-width/full-height cross. $W\equiv0$ outside the canton. So ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$; otherwise $W\equiv0$.

Thus
$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},$$
the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and the rank-one white-corner matrix. Hence
${\rm rk}M\le1+1=2$. For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types
$i\notin A$: $M_{i*}\equiv a$,
$i\in A$: $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$, $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and similarly for columns, so ${\rm rk}M=2$ generically. Up to translation the non-constant part is the familiar essential rank-one white picture, rank $1$ for $W$. The degenerate $a=b$ case gives ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ for the zero matrix.

The $R=J-C+H+V-O$ five-term writing is $J-R_c+H+V-O$ with $R_c=r c$, $H=h c$, $V=r v$, $O=h v$. The white indicator is $W=R_c-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$; the five rank-one pieces $J,R_c,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent, so the formal bound $1+4=5$ is not attained. The $J,R_c,X$ three-term rank $3$ argument treats the cross $X$ as an independent rank-one emblem; in the true Tongan cross $X=H+V-O$ is itself dependent on $R_c$, collapsing to the product above. The shield/disc/unbounded rank remarks refer to a different flag with a non-rectangular emblem; the actual Tongan flag has no such emblem.

Remaining point: the maximal rank over all admissible pixelations is $2$ for $a\ne b$, $1$ in the trivial constant case. The $1+1=2$ count is often quoted as essential rank $1$ for the white pattern. This agrees with Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 and refutes the rank $5$ and rank $3$ overcounting of Colleagues 10 and 7.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour Tonga picture is red field with a white hoist canton and a red St George cross inside the canton. Write $J_{ij}\equiv 1$, $r_i={\bf1}_{i\le h_c}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{j\le w_c}$ for the canton, $h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$ for the rows of the horizontal arm, $v_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ for the columns of the vertical arm. On the canton

${\bf1}_{{\rm red\;cross}}=r_i c_j\bigl(h_i+v_j-h_i v_j\bigr)$,

so with ${\bf1}_{R_c}=r_i c_j$

${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}= {\bf1}_{R_c}-{\bf1}_{{\rm red\;cross}}
 =r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j
 =(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)$.

Hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture, zero-padded outside the canton,

${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=\rho_i\sigma_j$ with
$\rho_i=r_i(1-h_i)={\bf1}_{A}(i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j(1-v_j)={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le h_c:i\notin H\}$,$B=\{j\le w_c:j\notin V\}$, i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner rectangles left by the cross. In particular ${\rm rk}\,{\bf1}_{{\rm white}}=1$ as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$ and ${\bf1}_{{\rm white}}\equiv0$ off the canton.

With $M_{ij}=a$ on red, $b$ on white,

$M_{ij}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a){\bf1}_{{\rm white}}(i,j)=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$,

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and a rank-one white-corner matrix. Hence

${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2$.

For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$, the two row types $i\notin A$ : $M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A$ : $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise, are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$; the non-constant part $(b-a){\bf1}_{{\rm white}}$ is essentially rank one. The degenerate $a=b$ case gives $M\equiv aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$.

The $J-C+H+V-O$ five-term formalisation $R=J-C+H+V-O$ is linearly dependent on the true cross: $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$, i.e. the five rank-one pieces collapse to $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$. The $3$-rank/$4$-block/5-rank claims arise from treating the emblem as a distinct rectangle/disc or from splitting $H$ and $V$ without the cancellation $H+V-O$, and from the shield/disc idealisation that is not present on the Tongan St George cross. The consensus of the present round is the $1+1$ description: essential rank one for the white pattern, total rank two for $M$ with $a\neq b$, rank one in the trivial $a=b$ case.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The colour matrix can be written up to translation as 
$M_{ij}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)W_{ij}$ with $W_{ij}=1$ on white and $0$ on red, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.

For the actual Tongan flag there is a red field, a white canton $R_c=\{i\le r_c\}\times\{j\le c_c\}$ and a red St George cross in the canton. Let 
$r_i={\bf1}_{i\le r_c},\;c_j={\bf1}_{j\le c_c}$,
$h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$ for the horizontal arm rows, $v_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ for the vertical arm columns. On the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_i c_j+r_i v_j-h_i v_j,$$
so
$$W_{ij}=r_i c_j-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j$$
with $\rho_i=r_i(1-h_i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j(1-v_j)$,
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton. 
$A=\{i:\rho_i=1\}$ is the rows of the canton outside the horizontal arm,
$B=\{j:\sigma_j=1\}$ the columns of the canton outside the vertical arm.
The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner rectangles of the canton, hence $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is rank one as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, the usual non-degenerate pixelation.

Thus
$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$
is the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and the rank-one white-corner matrix. Hence
${\rm rk}M\le2$, and for $a\neq b$ and $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$. For $a=b$, $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$,
$0$ in the zero case. Up to the inessential constant the non-constant part is rank one.

The five-piece decomposition $R=J-C+H+V-O$ used by Colleague 10 is linearly dependent here:
$W=C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$,
so $C,\,H,\,V,\,O$ span only a two-dimensional space together with $J$, not five.
The $3$-rank claims of Colleagues 2,3,4,6,7,8 arise from inserting a non-rectangular red emblem/shield/disc $C_c$ in the canton,
$W=R_c-C_c$, with $R_c$ rank one and $C_c$ in general rank $>1$, giving ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}R_c+{\rm rk}C_c$. That emblem is not present on the standard Tongan flag; the cross factorises as above, so the $H+V-O$ pieces cancel to a single rank-one factor and no unbounded growth occurs. With the true cross the rank is bounded and attained at $2$ for $a\neq b$.

Current consensus in the round: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 give the $1+1$ description with maximal ${\rm rk}M=2$, essentially ${\rm rk}W=1$. Colleague 10 insists on rank $5$ from the naive $J,C,H,V,O$ count, and Colleague 7 insists on rank $3$ from a single cross emblem model. The dependence $W=(r-h)(c-v)$ resolves the disagreement in favour of the rank-two picture. Unresolved in the literature is only the degenerate $a=b$ case giving rank $1$, which is the trivial maximal $2$ for $a\neq b$.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.  For the Tongan flag the white set is the hoist canton minus the red St George cross.  With $r_i={\bf1}_{i\le r_c}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{j\le c_c}$, $h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$,

\[
{\bf1}_{C}=r c^T,\quad {\bf1}_H=h c^T,\quad {\bf1}_V=r v^T,\quad {\bf1}_{H\cap V}=h v^T,
\]

and on the whole picture $W\equiv0$ off the canton and

\[
W_{ij}=r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j=(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,
\]
with $\rho_i=r_i(1-h_i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j(1-v_j)$.  Hence $W=\rho\sigma^T$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, $A=\{i\le r_c:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_c:j\notin V\}$, i.e. the four white corner rectangles left by the cross.  So ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Therefore

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^T,
\]

sum of two rank-one matrices. ${\rm rk}M\le2$, and for $a\ne b$ with a non-degenerate pixelation the two row types $i\notin A$: $M_{i*} \equiv a$ and $i\in A$: $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise, are independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$; the non-constant part is essentially rank one. The degenerate case $a=b$ gives ${\rm rk}M=1$.

This is the position of Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in both rounds.  Their factorisation $W=(r-h)(c-v)$ shows the five formal pieces $J,C,H,V,O$ used in $R=J-C+H+V-O$ are linearly dependent: $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$.

Colleague 10 and 7 push $5$ and $3$.  Colleague 10 writes $R=J-C+H+V-O$ as five axis-aligned rectangle indicators and claims independence, giving rank $\le5$, maximal $5$.  Colleague 7 keeps a single cross emblem $X$ and gets $M=aJ+(b-a)(C-X)$ hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, attained for a rectangular shield model.  The $3$–rank claims of Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8 are the idealised rectangle-minus-rectangular-hole model $W=uv^T-p^sq^{sT}$, i.e. $M=aJ+(b-a)(uv^T-p^sq^{sT})$, rank $\le3$, which is the rank of a canton with a single rectangular red emblem, not the actual couped cross.

The unbounded-rank remarks arise if the red emblem is taken as a genuine Euclidean disc/shield whose $0\!-\!1$ indicator is no longer rank-one; then ${\rm rk}M$ can be made arbitrarily large with refinement.  For the exact axis-aligned cross the product structure is exact and the rank stays bounded by $2$.

Unresolved nuance is only the modelling choice: strict pixel-aligned cross $\to$ maximal non-degenerate rank $2$, essentially $1$ for $W$; idealised rectangular shield $\to$ rank $3$; formal arm-by-arm counting $\to$ $5$ claims which overcount because $(r-h)(c-v)$ collapses the four corner rectangles to one rank-one product.  My current belief is the axis-aligned cross model, i.e. maximal possible rank $2$ for $a\neq b$, $1$ for $a=b$, with the $1$ non-trivial rank for the white pattern.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator. Up to the harmless constant $aJ$ the rank is that of $W$.

For Tonga the white set is the canton minus the red St George cross. With $r_i={\bf1}_{i\le r_c}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{j\le c_c}$, $h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$ for the horizontal arm and $v_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ for the vertical arm,

\[
{\bf1}_{\rm white}=r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j
      =(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,
\]
$\rho_i=r_i(1-h_i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j(1-v_j)$. Zero padded outside the canton $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$. Hence $W$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$ with $A=\{i:r_i=1,h_i=0\}$ and $B=\{j:c_j=1,v_j=0\}$, the four white corner rectangles left by the cross. So ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A,B\neq\varnothing$, the usual non-degenerate pixelation, and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.

Thus $M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices. ${\rm rk}M\le2$ and for $a\neq b$, $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types $i\notin A: M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A: M_{ij}=b$ on $B$, $a$ elsewhere are independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$. Modulo the constant background the non-trivial white part is rank one; $a=b$ gives the degenerate constant matrix ${\rm rk}=1$.

The $J-C+H+V-O$ five-term decomposition used by Colleague 10 is formally correct for the red indicator $R=J-C+H+V-O$, but the five rank-one pieces are linearly dependent for the cross:
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$. The collapse $ {\bf1}_{\rm white}= {\bf1}_{canton}-{\bf1}_{cross}=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ reduces the four pieces to a single rank-one white block. The $3$-rank claims of Colleagues 7,3,4,8 arise from treating the cross as a generic red emblem $X$ and writing $M=aJ+(b-a)(C-X)$ giving ${\rm rk}\le3$. That is the rank of a canton-minus-one-rectangular-hole idealisation, not the actual couped cross where the white set factorises.

The unbounded rank remarks are the disc/shield idealisation where ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{D}$ grows with resolution; the genuine Tongan cross is separable by rows and columns.

Current consensus in the round: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 argue ${\rm rk}M=2$ generically, essential rank one for $W$. Colleague 10 maintains maximal rank $5$ from the $J,C,H,V,O$ independence claim, and Colleague 7 maintains maximal rank $3$ from the $J,C,X$ block model. The dependence $(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ shows the $5$ and $3$ overcounts are due to forgetting the cancellation in the cross. Maximal attainable non-degenerate rank is $2$, $1$ up to the constant background, $1$ in the trivial $a=b$ case.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The colour matrix can be written $M_{ij}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)W_{ij}$ with $J\equiv1$ and $W=1$ on white, $0$ on red. Up to translation ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.

Let $u_i={\bf1}_{i\le r_c}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{j\le c_c}$ be the canton, $h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$ the rows of the red horizontal arm and $k_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ the columns of the red vertical arm, all in the canton. On the canton the red cross is $h_i v_j+u_i k_j-h_i k_j$ and

$$
W_{ij}=u_i v_j-h_i v_j-u_i k_j+h_i k_j=(u_i-h_i)(v_j-k_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,
$$

with $\rho_i=u_i(1-h_i)$, $\sigma_j=v_j(1-k_j)$, zero outside the canton. Hence

$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product 
$A\times B$, $A=\{i\le r_c:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_c:j\notin V\}$,

      =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\]

$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})=1_{A}(i)$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})=1_{B}(j)$.
$A$ is the set of canton rows left by the horizontal arm, $B$ the set of canton columns left by the vertical arm.  The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner rectangles of the canton, i.e. up to zero padding $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$.

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and one rank-one white-corner matrix.  Thus

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
\]

and for $a\neq b$ with $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types
$i\notin A$: $M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A$: $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise,

$W_{c}-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$,

That is the rank of a canton-minus-one-rectangular-hole idealisation, not the actual couped cross where the white set factorises.

The unbounded rank remarks are the disc/shield idealisation where ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{D}$ grows with resolution; the genuine Tongan cross is separable by rows and columns.

Current consensus in the round: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 argue ${\rm rk}M=2$ generically, essential rank one for $W$. Colleague 10 maintains maximal rank $5$ from the $J,C,H,V,O$ independence claim, and Colleague 7 maintains maximal rank $3$ from the $J,C,X$ block model. The dependence $(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ shows the $5$ and $3$ overcounts are due to forgetting the cancellation in the cross. Maximal attainable non-degenerate rank is $2$, $1$ up to the constant background, $1$ in the trivial $a=b$ case.
reflection_text.6:
The colour matrix can be written $M_{ij}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)W_{ij}$ with $J\equiv1$ and $W=1$ on white, $0$ on red. Up to translation ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.

Let $u_i={\bf1}_{i\le r_c}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{j\le c_c}$ be the canton, $h_i={\bf1}_{i\in H}$ the rows of the red horizontal arm and $k_j={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ the columns of the red vertical arm, all in the canton. On the canton the red cross is $h_i v_j+u_i k_j-h_i k_j$ and

$$
W_{ij}=u_i v_j-h_i v_j-u_i k_j+h_i k_j=(u_i-h_i)(v_j-k_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,
$$

with $\rho_i=u_i(1-h_i)$, $\sigma_j=v_j(1-k_j)$, zero outside the canton. Hence

$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product 
$A\times B$, $A=\{i\le r_c:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_c:j\notin V\}$,
the four white corner rectangles left by the cross. For a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ so ${\rm rk}W=1$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.

Thus

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}
$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le2$ and for $a\neq b$ the two row types $i\notin A$, $M_{i*} \equiv a$, and $i\in A$, $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$ and $a$ otherwise, are independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$. Modulo the constant background the non-trivial part is rank one. The degenerate case $a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$ with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the zero convention.

The $J-C+H+V-O$ five-term decomposition is linearly dependent: $C-H-V+O=(u-h)(v-k)^{T}$, i.e. $W_{c}=R_c-H-V+O$ collapses to the single outer product $\rho\sigma^{T}$. The $3$-rank/4-block statements are the rectangular-canton-minus-rectangular-emblem idealisation $M=aJ+(b-a)(uv^{T}-p^{s}q^{sT})$, i.e. a disc/shield $C_c$ in the canton, which is not the actual Tongan couped cross. The rank-5 claim likewise counts $J,C,H,V,O$ as independent; they are not independent on the true cross.

Consensus in the current round from Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is the $1+1$ description: essential rank one for the white pattern, total rank two for the two-level $a,b$ matrix. Colleague 10 persists with the formal $J-C+H+V-O$ count giving $\le5$, and Colleague 7 persists with the emblem $J,C,X$ count giving $\le3$. Both are idealisations that replace the couped cross by a single emblem/disc. The remaining open issue is only the terminology around the disc/shield idealisation; on the actual Tongan cross the maximal generic rank is $2$, essentially $1$, falling to $1$ for $a=b$.
reflection_text.2:
The two-colour matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J\equiv1$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  $ {\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.  For the Tongan flag the red field is the whole $m\times n$ picture, the white part is confined to the canton and the red part of the canton is the St George cross.

Let $r_{i}=1_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}$, $c_{j}=1_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ be the canton, $h_{i}=1_{\{i\in H\}}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and $v_{j}=1_{\{j\in V\}}$ the columns of the vertical arm.  On the canton
${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j}$ and with $W\equiv0$ off the canton

\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
      =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\]

$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})=1_{A}(i)$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})=1_{B}(j)$.
$A$ is the set of canton rows left by the horizontal arm, $B$ the set of canton columns left by the vertical arm.  The white set is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four corner rectangles of the canton, i.e. up to zero padding $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$.

Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A\neq\varnothing\neq B$, the usual non-degenerate pixelation, and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Then

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and one rank-one white-corner matrix.  Thus

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
\]

and for $a\neq b$ with $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two row types
$i\notin A$: $M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A$: $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$.  The non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one; modulo the inessential constant background the essential rank is $1$.  The degenerate case $a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the zero case.

The $J-W_{c}+H+V-O$ five term writing $R=J-C+H+V-O$ is formally $R_{c},H,V,O$ rank one, giving the crude bound $5$.  It is not sharp because
$W_{c}-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$,
so $R_{c},H,V,O$ are linearly dependent: $W_{c}-H-V+O$ is exactly $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  The $3$-rank proposals $M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)X$ with $X=H+V-O$ double count the same dependence; $C-X=W$ is already rank one.  The $3$-rank, $4$-rank, $5$-rank and unbounded disc/shield remarks correspond to replacing the exact rectangular cross by a non-rectangular emblem whose indicator rank grows with resolution.  With the geometric Tongan cross the cancellation is exact and the maximal attainable rank for a genuine two-colour discretisation is $2$, essentially $1$ for the white pattern, $1$ in the trivial $a=b$ case.

6.text:
Write $J_{ij}\equiv1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white. Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

so up to the harmless constant $aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ for the
white canton and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $k_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
be the indicator of the red horizontal and the red vertical arm of the
couped cross in the canton.  On the whole picture $W\equiv0$ outside the
canton and on the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}v_{j}+u_{i}k_{j}-h_{i}k_{j}, \qquad
{\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=u_{i}v_{j},$$

so that

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&=u_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j}-u_{i}k_{j}+h_{i}k_{j}\\
     &=\bigl(u_{i}-h_{i}\bigr)\bigl(v_{j}-k_{j}\bigr)
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{align*}
with $\rho_{i}=u_{i}(1-h_{i})$, $\sigma_{j}=v_{j}(1-k_{j})$, zero
outside the canton.  Put

$$A=\{i:\rho_{i}=1\}=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad 
  B=\{j:\sigma_{j}=1\}=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},$$

the rows of the canton not covered by the horizontal arm and the columns
of the canton not covered by the vertical arm.  Apart from zero padding

$$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four
white corner rectangles left by the couped cross.  For a non-degenerate
pixelation $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$ and

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},$$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank one matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2.$$

For $a\ne b$ the two geometric row types
$i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$, and
$i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so the bound is
attained.  Thus for the actual Tongan couped cross

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2\;{\rm for}\;a\ne b,$$

i.e. one non-trivial direction $\rho\sigma^{T}$ on the constant red
background $aJ$.  Up to the inessential translation $M\mapsto M-b$ the
non-constant part of the two-colour picture is essentially rank one.
In the degenerate case $a=b$, $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the
zero convention.  Modulo the constant background this is the familiar
$1+1$ description, the five rank-one pieces $J,C,H,V,O$ being linearly
dependent,
$C-H-V+O=(u-h)(v-k)^{T}=\rho\sigma^{T}$.  The $3$–$5$ rank counts are
the disc/emblem idealisations $J+C+X$ and $J-C+H+V-O$ in which the
couped cross is replaced by a single non-rectangular emblem. ∎

4.text:
With $J_{ij}\equiv1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ on white, $0$ on red,

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W,$$

and up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-b$ the rank is the rank
of the white indicator.  Put the canton on the hoist,

$$r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\qquad c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}},$$
and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ be the
horizontal and vertical arms of the red St George cross in the canton.
On the whole picture $W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},$$

so that

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
      =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}  \\
     &=(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{align*}

with 
$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$.
Hence, up to zero padding,

$$W=\rho\sigma^{T} ,$$

the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$; i.e. the four white
corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
the pixelation is non-degenerate, $A\ne\varnothing$, $B\ne\varnothing$,
and $W\equiv0$ on the red field.

Therefore

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank one matrix $J$ and the rank one
white-corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2,$$

and the bound is attained for $a\ne b$.  Indeed
$i\notin A$ gives $M_{i*}\equiv a$ whereas for $i\in A$,
$M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise; the two row types are
linearly independent for $a\ne b$, and the same for the columns.  Modulo
the inessential constant background $aJ$ the non-constant part
$(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one.

In the degenerate case $a=b$, $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the
zero case.  The $J,C,H,V,O$ five-term formalisation collapses because

$$W_{c}=C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T},$$

so $C,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent together with $J$.  Up to translation
the genuine two-colour Tongan picture is the familiar $1+1$ red
background $+$ white corner product, i.e. essential rank one, total rank
two for $a\ne b$.  This is the $1+1$ description and is the maximum
attainable. ∎

5.text:
With $J_{ij}\equiv1$ put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and
$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$.  Up to the harmless constant $aJ$
${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$.

Let $r_{i}= {\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}$, $c_{j}= {\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ be the
white canton and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of
the St George cross in the canton.  On the canton

${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j}$ ,

so that on the whole $m\times n$ picture, $W\equiv0$ off the canton,

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
     =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{equation*}

where
$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$ the canton rows left by the horizontal arm
and $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$ the canton columns left by the vertical
arm.  Thus

$W_{ij}=0$ off the canton and $W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j}$ on the canton,
i.e. $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product
$A\times B$, the four white corner rectangles of the canton.  In
particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ whenever $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$, the
ordinary non-degenerate pixelation, and $W\equiv0$ outside the canton.

Hence

$$
M_{ij}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
$$

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white-corner
matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$ and a genuine pixelation the two geometric row types
$i\notin A$, $M_{i*}\equiv a$, and $i\in A$, $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$, $M_{ij}=a$
otherwise, are linearly independent.  The same holds for the columns, so
${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained, e.g. with the usual two row-blocks and two
column-blocks.  Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the non-constant part
$(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one, the familiar red background plus the
white corner block $A\times B$.

In the degenerate case $a=b$ we have $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in
the zero convention.  Up to the trivial translation this is the usual
essential rank-one white pattern and total rank-two two-colour picture.
The five-term writing $R=J-C+H+V-O$ collapses to
$J+\rho\sigma^{T}$ because $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)$, so the pieces
$J,C,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent on the genuine Tongan couped cross.
This is the $1+1$, essentially rank one, description. ∎

9.text:
The two colour matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ where $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel.  Up to the inessential translation $M\mapsto M-bJ$
the rank is the rank of the white indicator.

Put $r_{i}={\mathbf 1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\mathbf 1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$
for the white canton and $h_{i}={\mathbf 1}_{\{i\in H\}},\;v_{j}
={\mathbf 1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ for the horizontal and the vertical arm of the red
St George cross in the canton.  On the whole $m\times n$ picture
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},
\]

hence

\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
      =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\]

with $\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})$.
Put $A=\{i:\rho_{i}=1\}$ and $B=\{j:\sigma_{j}=1\}$.  $A$ is the set of
canton rows not covered by the horizontal arm and $B$ the set of canton
columns not covered by the vertical arm.  The white set in the canton is
the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four white corner rectangles
left by the couped cross, and after zero padding

\[
W=\rho\sigma^{T},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1\qquad A\neq\varnothing\neq B .
\]

Hence on the whole picture

\[
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
\]

and for a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ and $a\ne b$
the two geometric row types

* $i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$,
* $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b\;{\rm for}\;j\in B,\;M_{ij}=a\;{\rm otherwise},$

are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the
harmless constant $aJ$, i.e. for the white indicator $W$, the non-trivial
part of the flag is the familiar essentially rank-one $A\times B$
product.  In the degenerate case $a=b$, $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$.
The $J-C+H+V-O$ five term writing is $M=aJ+(b-a)(C-H-V+O)$ with
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$; the five rank-one pieces are linearly
dependent and collapse to the $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$ description above.
This is the $1+1$ rank, essentially rank one, quoted by Colleagues 1-6,8-9. ∎

8.text:
The two colour matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel is
white and $J_{ij}\equiv 1$.  Up to the harmless constant $aJ$ the rank is
the rank of the white indicator.

Put $r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ for the
white canton and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$ and $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in
V\}}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical
arm of the red St George cross in the canton.  On the whole picture
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

\[
{\bf1}_{C}=r_{i}c_{j},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{H}=h_{i}c_{j},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{V}=r_{i}v_{j},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{H\cap V}=h_{i}v_{j},
\]

so that the white part of the canton is

\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{ij}&=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}  \\
     &=\bigl(r_{i}-h_{i}\bigr)\bigl(c_{j}-v_{j}\bigr)
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{aligned}
\]

with
$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$.
Hence, up to zero padding,
\[
W=\rho\sigma^{T},
\]
the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four white
corner rectangles left by the cross.  In particular

\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1\qquad A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing,
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  The five formal rectangle indicators
$J,C,H,V,O=H\cap V$ satisfy
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ so that $J,C,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent.
Put

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-one rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white-corner
matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le \operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\]

and the two directions are the constant red background and the
white-corner product $A\times B$.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the
two geometric row types
$i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$,
$i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so that
$\operatorname{rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the inessential constant
$aJ$ the non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one.  The
degenerate case $a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$ and $\operatorname{rk}M=1$.

In the usual statement the essential two-colour rank of the Tongan flag
is $1$, i.e. $1+1=2$ with the constant background counted, which is the
$J+\rho\sigma^{T}$ description.  The $3$– and $5$–rank counts are obtained
by treating the cross as a single non-rectangular emblem $X$ or by
keeping the five rectangle indicators $J,C,H,V,O$ formally independent;
on the exact axis-aligned couped cross $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ and the
formal five terms collapse to the $1+1$ picture above. ∎

1.text:
Write $J_{ij}\equiv1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ on white, $0$ on red.  On the whole
$m\times n$ picture
$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
$$
so up to the harmless $aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.

Put $r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ for the
white canton and $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}},\,v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
for the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of
the red St George cross in the canton.  On the canton

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},
\qquad 
{\bf1}_{R_{c}}=r_{i}c_{j}.
\]

Outside the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton
\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}).
\]
Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

\[
A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad 
B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},
\]

the rows and columns of the canton left by the horizontal and the
vertical arm.  Then, up to zero padding off the canton,

\[
W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four white corner rectangles left by the cross.  Hence

\[
{\rm rk}W=1\qquad A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing,
\]
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Now

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Thus

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
\]

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two
geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$,
$M_{ij}=a$ otherwise, are linearly independent, and the same for the
columns, so ${\rm rk}M=2$, i.e. one dimension for the constant red
background $aJ$ and one non-trivial dimension for the white corner
product $A\times B$.  Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the
non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is the familiar essentially rank-one white
picture, ${\rm rk}W=1$.

In particular $R_{c},H,V,O$ are linearly dependent,
$W_{c}=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$, so the formal five-term decomposition
$J-R_{c}+H+V-O$ collapses to $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$.  The degenerate
$a=b$ case gives the constant matrix $M\equiv aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$.
Up to the trivial background this is the usual essential rank one,
i.e. rank two for the two-colour matrix $M$ with $a\ne b$.  The
rank $3,4,5$ counts are obtained by artificially splitting the cross and
forgetting the cancellation $W=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$. ∎

3.text:
Write $J_{ij}\equiv1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then
on the two colour scale

$$M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,$$

and up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-b$ the rank is the rank
of the white indicator.  Let $r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}$,
$c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ be the canton and let
$h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ be the horizontal
and vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.  On the whole picture
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},$$

so that

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}\\
     &=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}  \\
     &=(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
\end{align*}

Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$,

the rows of the canton not covered by the horizontal arm and the
columns of the canton not covered by the vertical arm.  Then, up to zero
padding,

$$W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},$$

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four corner rectangles left by the cross.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing$, and
$W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one
white-corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.

Therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2.$$

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the two
geometric row types

* $i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$,
* $i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,

are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so
${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the harmless constant background
$aJ$ the non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is the familiar essentially
rank-one white corner block $A\times B$.

In the degenerate case $a=b$ the matrix is constant, ${\rm rk}M=1$,
and $0$ in the zero convention.  Up to the inessential constant this is
the usual essential rank one for the white pattern and total rank two
for the $a,b$ coloured matrix.  The formal five term decomposition
$J-R_{c}+H+V-O$ collapses because
$-R_{c}+H+V-O=-(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$, so $J,R_{c},H,V,O$ are linearly
dependent and the genuine two-colour Tongan picture is $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$.
This is the $1+1$ rank quoted above; the $3,4,5$ counts arise from
treating the cross as a generic non-rectangular emblem whose indicator
rank can grow with the resolution.  The actual Tongan cross is the
full-width/full-height couped cross, whose white complement factorises. ∎

2.text:
Write $J_{ij}\equiv 1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Up to
the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-bJ$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
\end{equation*}
so up to the constant background the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.

Put the canton on the hoist,
$r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$.
Let $H\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ be the rows of the red horizontal arm
and $V\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ the columns of the red vertical arm in
the canton and put $h_{i}={\bf1}_{H}(i),\;v_{j}={\bf1}_{V}(j)$.  On the
whole $m\times n$ picture $W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=r_{i}c_{j}.
\]

Hence

\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}),\qquad 1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n,
\]

with the convention $W_{ij}=0$ off the canton.  Put

\[
\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\qquad 
\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j),
\]

$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$ the canton rows left by the horizontal arm
and $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$ the canton columns left by the vertical
arm.  Then $W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j}$ on the whole lattice, i.e. up to
zero padding

\[
W=\rho\sigma^{T}
\]

is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four white
corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular

\[
{\rm rk}W=1\qquad A\ne\varnothing\ne B,
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank one matrix $J$ and the rank one white
corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
\]

For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the
two geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and
$M_{ij}=a$ otherwise are linearly independent, and the same holds for
the columns, so that

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,
\]

is attained.  Modulo the inessential constant background $aJ$ the
non-constant white part of the Tongan flag is the single rank-one
product $A\times B$; with the background counted the two-colour matrix
is generically of rank two, rank one in the degenerate $a=b$ case,
$0$ for the zero matrix.  Up to the trivial constant this is the usual
essential rank one of the white canton-minus-cross pattern.  The
$J-C+H+V-O$ five term writing collapses because
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ is already rank one, so the formal $5$-term
bound is not sharp. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I remain with the rank \(2\) conclusion. The key is to work with the two-colour matrix, not with heraldic components. Write
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white indicator. The white region is the canton minus the red cross. Whether one describes the cross as couped or not, the removal is by a row cut and a column cut inside the canton, so up to zero padding outside the canton,
\[
W=(r-h)(c-v)^T,
\]
a single rank-one product. C10’s expansion
\[
R=J-C+H+V-O
\]
is only an intermediate five-term description before cancellation. Those five rank-one pieces are not independent in the sum: the canton and the cross arms satisfy
\[
C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^T,
\]
so the advertised five directions collapse to one non-constant direction. Rank of a sum is not additive over an arbitrary decomposition. Likewise C7’s \(3\) double-counts the canton and the cross as separate directions when one is already the complement of the other inside the canton. Thus for \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate pixelation, the matrix is a constant background plus one rank-one white-corner term, giving maximum rank \(2\).

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the rank \(2\) factorization. Colleague 10’s rank \(5\) counts the five rectangle indicators \(J,C,H,V,O\) as if they were independent colour directions, but the actual matrix only records red versus white. Substituting \(R=J-C+H+V-O\) into \(M=aR+bW\) gives
\[
W=C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)=\rho\sigma^T,
\]
so the two arms and the overlap correction are not independent: the overlap is exactly the correction that collapses the cross complement into a single rank-one product. The same cancellation also removes Colleague 7’s proposed third direction: the red cross is not an extra colour class on top of the canton; it is precisely the zero set of \(W\) inside the canton.

Thus, with \(J\) the all-ones matrix,
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^T
\]
is the sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a non-degenerate pixelation the two directions are independent, so the maximal possible rank is \(2\). The couped-cross objection changes which row and column sets enter \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\), but it does not create an additional independent rank direction in the final red/white matrix.

public_text.6:
Write $J_{ij}\equiv1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white. Then

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

so up to the harmless constant $aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ for the
white canton and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $k_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
be the indicator of the red horizontal and the red vertical arm of the
couped cross in the canton.  On the whole picture $W\equiv0$ outside the
canton and on the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}v_{j}+u_{i}k_{j}-h_{i}k_{j}, \qquad
{\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=u_{i}v_{j},$$

so that

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&=u_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j}-u_{i}k_{j}+h_{i}k_{j}\\
     &=\bigl(u_{i}-h_{i}\bigr)\bigl(v_{j}-k_{j}\bigr)
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{align*}
with $\rho_{i}=u_{i}(1-h_{i})$, $\sigma_{j}=v_{j}(1-k_{j})$, zero
outside the canton.  Put

$$A=\{i:\rho_{i}=1\}=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad 
  B=\{j:\sigma_{j}=1\}=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},$$

the rows of the canton not covered by the horizontal arm and the columns
of the canton not covered by the vertical arm.  Apart from zero padding

$$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four
white corner rectangles left by the couped cross.  For a non-degenerate
pixelation $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$ and

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},$$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank one matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2.$$

For $a\ne b$ the two geometric row types
$i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$, and
$i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so the bound is
attained.  Thus for the actual Tongan couped cross

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2\;{\rm for}\;a\ne b,$$

i.e. one non-trivial direction $\rho\sigma^{T}$ on the constant red
background $aJ$.  Up to the inessential translation $M\mapsto M-b$ the
non-constant part of the two-colour picture is essentially rank one.
In the degenerate case $a=b$, $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the
zero convention.  Modulo the constant background this is the familiar
$1+1$ description, the five rank-one pieces $J,C,H,V,O$ being linearly
dependent,
$C-H-V+O=(u-h)(v-k)^{T}=\rho\sigma^{T}$.  The $3$–$5$ rank counts are
the disc/emblem idealisations $J+C+X$ and $J-C+H+V-O$ in which the
couped cross is replaced by a single non-rectangular emblem. ∎
public_text.4:

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W,$$

and up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-b$ the rank is the rank
of the white indicator.  Put the canton on the hoist,

$$r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\qquad c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}},$$

so that

\begin{align*}
W_{ij}&=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
      =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}  \\

\end{align*}

with 
$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,

Hence, up to zero padding,

$$W=\rho\sigma^{T} ,$$

the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$; i.e. the four white
corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as
the pixelation is non-degenerate, $A\ne\varnothing$, $B\ne\varnothing$,
and $W\equiv0$ on the red field.

With $J_{ij}\equiv1$ put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and

${\rm rk}M=1+{\rm rk}W$.

Let $r_{i}= {\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}}$, $c_{j}= {\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ be the
white canton and let $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of
the St George cross in the canton.  On the canton

${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j}$ ,

so that on the whole $m\times n$ picture, $W\equiv0$ off the canton,

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
     =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\end{equation*}

where
$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$ the canton rows left by the horizontal arm
and $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$ the canton columns left by the vertical
arm.  Thus

$W_{ij}=0$ off the canton and $W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j}$ on the canton,
i.e. $W=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product
$A\times B$, the four white corner rectangles of the canton.  In
particular

$$
M_{ij}=aJ_{ij}+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
$$

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white-corner

otherwise, are linearly independent.  The same holds for the columns, so

The two colour matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ where $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel.  Up to the inessential translation $M\mapsto M-bJ$
the rank is the rank of the white indicator.

Put $r_{i}={\mathbf 1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\mathbf 1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$
for the white canton and $h_{i}={\mathbf 1}_{\{i\in H\}},\;v_{j}
={\mathbf 1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ for the horizontal and the vertical arm of the red
St George cross in the canton.  On the whole $m\times n$ picture
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

\[

\]

hence

\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
      =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
      =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
\]

with $\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})$.

canton rows not covered by the horizontal arm and $B$ the set of canton
columns not covered by the vertical arm.  The white set in the canton is
the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four white corner rectangles
left by the couped cross, and after zero padding

\[

\]

\[
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},

are linearly independent, so ${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the

$\rho_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})={\bf1}_{B}(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$.
Hence, up to zero padding,
\[
W=\rho\sigma^{T},
\]
the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four white
corner rectangles left by the cross.  In particular

\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1\qquad A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing,
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  The five formal rectangle indicators
$J,C,H,V,O=H\cap V$ satisfy
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ so that $J,C,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent.
Put

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-one rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white-corner
matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le \operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\]

and the two directions are the constant red background and the
white-corner product $A\times B$.

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the
two geometric row types
$i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$,
$i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so that
$\operatorname{rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the inessential constant
$aJ$ the non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one.  The
degenerate case $a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$ and $\operatorname{rk}M=1$.

In the usual statement the essential two-colour rank of the Tongan flag
is $1$, i.e. $1+1=2$ with the constant background counted, which is the
$J+\rho\sigma^{T}$ description.  The $3$– and $5$–rank counts are obtained
by treating the cross as a single non-rectangular emblem $X$ or by
keeping the five rectangle indicators $J,C,H,V,O$ formally independent;
on the exact axis-aligned couped cross $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ and the
formal five terms collapse to the $1+1$ picture above. ∎

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
$$
so up to the harmless $aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.

white canton and $h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}},\,v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$
for the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of
the red St George cross in the canton.  On the canton

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},
\qquad 
{\bf1}_{R_{c}}=r_{i}c_{j}.
\]

Outside the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton
\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}).
\]
Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

\[
A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad 
B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},
\]

the rows and columns of the canton left by the horizontal and the
vertical arm.  Then, up to zero padding off the canton,

\[
W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four white corner rectangles left by the cross.  Hence

\[
{\rm rk}W=1\qquad A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing,
\]
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Now

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Thus

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
\]

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two
geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$,
$M_{ij}=a$ otherwise, are linearly independent, and the same for the
columns, so ${\rm rk}M=2$, i.e. one dimension for the constant red

Write $J_{ij}\equiv1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,$$

and up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-b$ the rank is the rank

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},$$

so that

\begin{align*}

     &=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}  \\
     &=(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
\end{align*}

Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$,

the rows of the canton not covered by the horizontal arm and the
columns of the canton not covered by the vertical arm.  Then, up to zero
padding,

$$W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},$$

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four corner rectangles left by the cross.  In particular
${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing$, and
$W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one
white-corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.

Therefore

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2.$$

For $a\ne b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the two
geometric row types

* $i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$,
* $i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,

are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so
${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the harmless constant background

rank-one white corner block $A\times B$.

Write $J_{ij}\equiv 1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white.  Up to

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}
so up to the constant background the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.

Put the canton on the hoist,
$r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$.
Let $H\subset\{1,\dots ,r_{c}\}$ be the rows of the red horizontal arm
and $V\subset\{1,\dots ,c_{c}\}$ the columns of the red vertical arm in
the canton and put $h_{i}={\bf1}_{H}(i),\;v_{j}={\bf1}_{V}(j)$.  On the
whole $m\times n$ picture $W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

\[
{\bf1}_{{\rm red}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=r_{i}c_{j}.
\]

Hence

\[
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}),\qquad 1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n,
\]

with the convention $W_{ij}=0$ off the canton.  Put

\[
\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\qquad 
\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j),
\]

$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\}$ the canton rows left by the horizontal arm
and $B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\}$ the canton columns left by the vertical
arm.  Then $W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j}$ on the whole lattice, i.e. up to
zero padding

\[
W=\rho\sigma^{T}
\]

is the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four white
corner rectangles of the canton.  In particular

\[
{\rm rk}W=1\qquad A\ne\varnothing\ne B,
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T},
\]

the sum of the all-ones rank one matrix $J$ and the rank one white
corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
\]

For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the
two geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$ and
$M_{ij}=a$ otherwise are linearly independent, and the same holds for
the columns, so that

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,
\]

is attained.  Modulo the inessential constant background $aJ$ the
non-constant white part of the Tongan flag is the single rank-one
product $A\times B$; with the background counted the two-colour matrix

essential rank one of the white canton-minus-cross pattern.  The
$J-C+H+V-O$ five term writing collapses because
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ is already rank one, so the formal $5$-term
bound is not sharp. ∎

I remain with the rank \(2\) conclusion. The key is to work with the two-colour matrix, not with heraldic components. Write
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white indicator. The white region is the canton minus the red cross. Whether one describes the cross as couped or not, the removal is by a row cut and a column cut inside the canton, so up to zero padding outside the canton,
\[
W=(r-h)(c-v)^T,
\]
a single rank-one product. C10’s expansion
\[
R=J-C+H+V-O
\]
is only an intermediate five-term description before cancellation. Those five rank-one pieces are not independent in the sum: the canton and the cross arms satisfy
\[
C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^T,
\]
so the advertised five directions collapse to one non-constant direction. Rank of a sum is not additive over an arbitrary decomposition. Likewise C7’s \(3\) double-counts the canton and the cross as separate directions when one is already the complement of the other inside the canton. Thus for \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate pixelation, the matrix is a constant background plus one rank-one white-corner term, giving maximum rank \(2\).

I agree with the rank \(2\) factorization. Colleague 10’s rank \(5\) counts the five rectangle indicators \(J,C,H,V,O\) as if they were independent colour directions, but the actual matrix only records red versus white. Substituting \(R=J-C+H+V-O\) into \(M=aR+bW\) gives
\[
W=C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)=\rho\sigma^T,
\]
so the two arms and the overlap correction are not independent: the overlap is exactly the correction that collapses the cross complement into a single rank-one product. The same cancellation also removes Colleague 7’s proposed third direction: the red cross is not an extra colour class on top of the canton; it is precisely the zero set of \(W\) inside the canton.

Thus, with \(J\) the all-ones matrix,
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^T
\]
is the sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}M\le 2\). For \(a\ne b\) and a non-degenerate pixelation the two directions are independent, so the maximal possible rank is \(2\). The couped-cross objection changes which row and column sets enter \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\), but it does not create an additional independent rank direction in the final red/white matrix.

1.text:
Write $J_{ij}\equiv 1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ on white, $0$ on red.  Then

$$
M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W ,
$$

so up to the harmless constant $aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white
indicator.  Put the canton on the hoist,
$r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ and let
$h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}},\;v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ be the rows of the
horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the red St George
cross in the canton.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},
$$

so that

$$
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j})
     =\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},
$$

with

$$
\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i),\qquad 
\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j),
$$

$$
A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},
$$

the canton rows and columns left by the two arms.  Up to zero padding
off the canton

$$
W=\rho\sigma^{T},
$$

the indicator of the Cartesian product $A\times B$, i.e. the four white
corner rectangles left by the couped cross.  Hence for a non-degenerate
pixelation $A\neq\varnothing$, $B\neq\varnothing$,

$$
{\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton}.
$$

Now

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}
$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
$$

For $a\ne b$ and $A,B\neq\varnothing$ the two geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and
$i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$, $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, and the same for the columns, so the bound
is attained:

$$
{\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2\;\;{\rm for}\;a\ne b,
$$

i.e. one dimension for the constant red background $aJ$ and one
non-trivial dimension for the white corner product $A\times B$.  Modulo
the inessential translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the non-constant white part
$(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one.  In the degenerate case $a=b$,
$M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $0$ in the zero convention.  The formal
$J-C+H+V-O$ five-term writing collapses because
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}=\rho\sigma^{T}$, so $J,C,H,V,O$ are linearly
dependent and the genuine two-colour Tongan matrix is $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$,
essential rank one, total rank two for $a\ne b$. ∎

2.text:
The two colour matrix can be written on the $m\times n$ lattice as

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad J_{ij}\equiv 1,$$

$W_{ij}=1$ on white and $0$ on red.  Up to the harmless translation
$M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator and
${\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W$.

Put the canton on the hoist
$r_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_{c}\}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_{c}\}}$ and let
$h_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ be the rows of the
red horizontal arm and the columns of the red vertical arm of the St
George cross in the canton.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},$$

so that

$$W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
      =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
      =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .$$

Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

$$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},$$

the canton rows left by the horizontal arm and the canton columns left
by the vertical arm.  Up to zero padding off the canton

$$W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},$$

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four white corner rectangles left by the couped cross.  Hence for a
non-degenerate pixelation $A\neq\varnothing\neq B$

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\ {\rm off\ the\ canton},$$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2,$$

and the bound is sharp.  For $a\neq b$ the two geometric row types
$i\notin A:$ $M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:$ $M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$,
$M_{ij}=a$ otherwise, are linearly independent, and the same for the
columns, so ${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained.  Modulo the inessential constant
background $aJ$ the non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one,
${\rm rk}W=1$.

In particular $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}$ so the formal five-term writing
$J-R_{c}+H+V-O$ collapses to $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$; $J,R_{c},H,V,O$ are
linearly dependent on the exact axis-aligned couped cross.  The
degenerate $a=b$ case gives the constant matrix $M\equiv aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$,
$0$ in the zero convention.  Up to translation this is the usual
essential rank-one white picture, total rank two for the two-colour
matrix with $a\neq b$. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the rank \(2\) consensus, and I think the key is to separate the two-colour matrix from any heraldic decomposition. The matrix is
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white indicator. Once \(W\) is the white indicator, the red cross is just the zero set of \(W\) inside the canton. Writing that zero set as \(C-H-V+O\) is an intermediate rectangle-counting device, not an independent decomposition of the final matrix: the overlap correction is exactly what makes the rectangle terms collapse. The couped-vs-non-couped point changes the support sets in \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\), but it does not add a new independent colour direction, because the final matrix still has only the constant background and one non-constant white term. Hence
\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1
\]
in the nondegenerate case and
\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le 1+1=2;

5.text:
With $J_{ij}\equiv 1$ let $W_{ij}=1$ on white and $0$ on red. Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
$$

so up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank
of the white indicator.

Put $r_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le h_{c}},\;c_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le w_{c}}$ for the canton
and $h_{i}={\bf1}_{i\in H},\,v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\in V}$ for the rows of the
horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the red St George
cross in the canton.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},
\qquad
{\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=r_{i}c_{j},
$$

hence

$$
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
$$

Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}
={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

$$
A=\{i\le h_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad 
B=\{j\le w_{c}:j\notin V\},
$$

the canton rows and columns left by the cross.  Then up to zero padding
off the canton

$$
W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},
$$

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four white corner rectangles left by the couped cross.  For a
non-degenerate pixelation $A,B\ne\varnothing$

$$
{\rm rk}W=1 ,
$$

and $W\equiv0$ on the red field.  Hence

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}=aJ+(b-a)W,
$$

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one
white-corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  In particular

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
$$

For $a\ne b$ and $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the two geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and $i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$,

attained.  Modulo the inessential constant background $aJ$ the
non-constant part $(b-a)W$ is essentially rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$.

constant this is the usual $1+1$, essentially rank-one, two-colour

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the rank \(2\) conclusion. The important point is not the heraldic shape of the cross but the algebraic form of the final two-colour matrix. Let \(W_{ij}=1\) on white and \(0\) on red. Then
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
so the only possible non-constant direction comes from \(W\). Inside the white canton the red cross, couped or not, is cut out by a row mask \(h_i\) and a column mask \(v_j\), and the overlap is exactly the correction term:
\[
W=C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^T
\]
after zero padding outside the canton. Thus the five formal pieces \(J,C,H,V,O\) are not independent colour directions; the overlap term \(O\) precisely cancels the apparent extra rank from the two arms. Hence \(W\) is a single outer product, so \(\operatorname{rank}W\le 1\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}M\le \operatorname{rank}J+\operatorname{rank}W\le 2.
\]
For \(a\ne b\) and a non-degenerate pixelation the constant red background and the white-corner product are independent, so the maximum is \(2\). I agree with the rank \(2\) consensus, and I think the key is to separate the two-colour matrix from any heraldic decomposition. The matrix is
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(W\) is the white indicator. Once \(W\) is the white indicator, the red cross is just the zero set of \(W\) inside the canton. Writing that zero set as \(C-H-V+O\) is an intermediate rectangle-counting device, not an independent decomposition of the final matrix: the overlap correction is exactly what makes the rectangle terms collapse. The couped-vs-non-couped point changes the support sets in \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\), but it does not add a new independent colour direction, because the final matrix still has only the constant background and one non-constant white term. Hence
\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1
\]
in the nondegenerate case and
\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le 1+1=2;
\]
for \(a\ne b\) the two directions are independent, so the maximal rank is \(2\). The \(4\) or \(5\) counts are over-counting rank-one rectangle indicators before cancellation, i.e. assuming rank is additive over a non-independent decomposition. I would keep the final answer at \(2\).

Write $J_{ij}\equiv 1$ and $W_{ij}=1$ on white, $0$ on red. Then

$$
M_{ij}=a(1-W_{ij})+bW_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W,
$$

so up to the harmless translation $M\mapsto M-aJ$ the rank is the rank of
the white indicator.

Put the canton on the hoist $r_{i}= {\bf1}_{i\le r_{c}}$,
$c_{j}= {\bf1}_{j\le c_{c}}$ and let $h_{i}= {\bf1}_{i\in H}$,
$v_{j}= {\bf1}_{j\in V}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns
of the vertical arm of the red St George cross in the canton.  Off the
canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j},\qquad
{\bf1}_{{\rm canton}}=r_{i}c_{j},
$$

hence on the whole $m\times n$ picture with zero padding off the canton

$$
W_{ij}=r_{i}c_{j}-{\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}
     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
$$

Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$,
$\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}={\bf1}_{B}(j)$ with

$$
A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},
$$

the canton rows and columns left by the two arms.  Then

$$
W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},
$$

i.e. the white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$,
the four white corner rectangles left by the couped cross.  Up to zero
padding $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  For a non-degenerate pixelation
$A\ne\varnothing,\;B\ne\varnothing$

$$
{\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}=aJ+(b-a)W
$$

is the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one
white-corner matrix $\rho\sigma^{T}$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le2 .
$$

For $a\ne b$ and $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the two geometric row types
$i\notin A:\;M_{i*}\equiv a$ and
$i\in A:\;M_{ij}=b$ for $j\in B$, $M_{ij}=a$ otherwise,
are linearly independent, so the bound is attained,
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$.  Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the
non-constant white part is essentially rank one.  In the degenerate
$a=b$ case $M\equiv aJ$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$, and if $A$ or $B$ is empty the
same rank $1$ is obtained.  In particular $C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}
=\rho\sigma^{T}$ so the formal five term $J-C+H+V-O$ collapses to
$J+\rho\sigma^{T}$; $J,C,H,V,O$ are linearly dependent on the exact
axis-aligned couped cross.  This is the $1+1$ red background plus white
corner product, i.e. essential rank one, total two-colour rank two for

of the white indicator and ${\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W$.

canton

$${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_{i}c_{j}+r_{i}v_{j}-h_{i}v_{j} .$$

     =r_{i}c_{j}-h_{i}c_{j}-r_{i}v_{j}+h_{i}v_{j}
     =(r_{i}-h_{i})(c_{j}-v_{j}) .
$$

Put $\rho_{i}=r_{i}-h_{i}={\bf1}_{A}(i)$, $\sigma_{j}=c_{j}-v_{j}

$$A=\{i\le r_{c}:i\notin H\},\qquad B=\{j\le c_{c}:j\notin V\},$$

the canton rows and columns left by the two arms.  Then

$$W_{ij}=\rho_{i}\sigma_{j},\qquad W=\rho\sigma^{T},$$

product $A\times B$, the four white corner rectangles left by the couped
cross.  For a non-degenerate pixelation $A\ne\varnothing$, $B\ne\varnothing$

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$$

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}\rho\sigma^{T}\le 2,$$

and for $a\ne b$ and $A,B\ne\varnothing$ the two geometric row types

otherwise, are linearly independent.  So the bound is attained:
${\rm rk}W=1$ and ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$.  Modulo the inessential
constant background $aJ$ the non-constant white part is essentially
rank one, $M-aJ=(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$.  In the degenerate constant case

formal five-term $J-C+H+V-O$ writing collapses because
$C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}=\rho\sigma^{T}$, so $J,C,H,V,O$ are linearly
dependent and the genuine two-colour Tongan matrix is $J+\rho\sigma^{T}$,
i.e. total rank two for $a\ne b$, essential rank one. ∎
