I agree with the rank \(2\) consensus. The key invariant is the final red/white matrix
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]
where \(J\) is all ones and \(W\) is the white indicator. Thus, after removing the constant red background, every nonconstant direction must come from \(W\). The cross in the canton is cut out by row and column masks; the inclusion-exclusion correction is precisely the overlap term, so the white part reduces to a single outer-product direction. The couped-vs-non-couped detail changes the supports of those masks, but it does not add an independent colour direction to the final two-colour matrix. Hence \(\operatorname{rank}W\le 1\), so
\[
\operatorname{rank}M\le \operatorname{rank}J+\operatorname{rank}W\le 1+1=2.
\]
For \(a\ne b\) and a nondegenerate pixelation, the constant background and the white direction are independent, so the maximum is \(2\). Counts like \(3,4,5\) arise only by treating \(J,C,H,V,O\) as independent before the cancellation \(C-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^T\), which overcounts the actual rank. I would keep the final answer at \(2\).

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,

the only non-constant component is the white indicator \(W\). The red cross inside the canton is cut out by a row mask and a column mask; taking the white complement gives the overlap correction

\[

\]

but in the actual two-colour matrix that cancellation removes the apparent extra directions. Thus the maximal possible rank is \(2\).

cross removed. With $r_i={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_c\}}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_c\}}$ for
the canton and $h_i={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ for the
horizontal and vertical arms,

${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_i c_j+r_i v_j-h_i v_j$ on the canton and
$W\equiv0$ off the canton. Hence

$W_{ij}=r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j=(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,$

$\rho_i=r_i-h_i={\bf1}_A(i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j-v_j={\bf1}_B(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_c:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_c:j\notin V\}$.
The white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four
corner rectangles left by the couped cross, i.e. up to zero padding
$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$.

Thus ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A\neq\varnothing\neq B$, the usual
non-degenerate pixelation, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$,

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and one rank-one white-corner
matrix. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le2$. For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation the two geometric row types $i\notin A$: $M_{i*}\equiv a$ and
$i\in A$: $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise, are linearly independent,
so ${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained. Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the
non-constant part is essentially rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$. The degenerate
case $a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, and $A$ or $B$ empty also
gives rank $1$.

The formal five-term writing $R=J-R_c+H+V-O$ collapses because
$R_c-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is already rank one; $J,R_c,H,V,O$
are linearly dependent on the exact axis-aligned couped cross. The $3,4,5$
and unbounded ranks arise from replacing the cross by a non-rectangular
emblem e.g. a disc/shield whose $0\!-\!1$ indicator has rank growing with
resolution, or from treating the five rectangle indicators as independent
before cancellation. The current round consensus of colleagues 1-10 is
unanimous for the St George couped cross model: maximal rank $2$ for
$a\neq b$, essential rank $1$ for the white pattern, $1$ in the trivial
$a=b$ or degenerate pixelation case. Colleague 10’s earlier rank-5 claim
is now retracted as over-counting of non-independent rectangle indicators.
The rectangular shield idealisation gives the often quoted $1+2=3$ total
rank, $2$ non-constant, and the true geometric disc gives unbounded rank
in the infinite resolution limit, but those are different models from the
actual couped cross of the Tongan flag.

reflection_text.2:
The matrix can be written up to translation as
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J\equiv1$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so
${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$ and the non-trivial rank is that of $W$.

For the real Tongan flag the red field is the whole $m\times n$ picture and
the white part is confined to the canton with the red St George couped
cross removed. With $r_i={\bf1}_{\{i\le r_c\}}$, $c_j={\bf1}_{\{j\le c_c\}}$ for
the canton and $h_i={\bf1}_{\{i\in H\}}$, $v_j={\bf1}_{\{j\in V\}}$ for the
horizontal and vertical arms,

${\bf1}_{{\rm cross}}=h_i c_j+r_i v_j-h_i v_j$ on the canton and
$W\equiv0$ off the canton. Hence

$W_{ij}=r_i c_j-h_i c_j-r_i v_j+h_i v_j=(r_i-h_i)(c_j-v_j)=\rho_i\sigma_j,$

$\rho_i=r_i-h_i={\bf1}_A(i)$, $\sigma_j=c_j-v_j={\bf1}_B(j)$,
$A=\{i\le r_c:i\notin H\}$, $B=\{j\le c_c:j\notin V\}$.
The white set in the canton is the Cartesian product $A\times B$, the four
corner rectangles left by the couped cross, i.e. up to zero padding
$W=\rho\sigma^{T}$.

Thus ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as $A\neq\varnothing\neq B$, the usual
non-degenerate pixelation, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)\rho\sigma^{T}$,

the sum of the all-ones rank-one matrix and one rank-one white-corner
matrix. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le2$. For $a\neq b$ and a non-degenerate
pixelation the two geometric row types $i\notin A$: $M_{i*}\equiv a$ and
$i\in A$: $M_{ij}=b$ on $j\in B$, $a$ otherwise, are linearly independent,
so ${\rm rk}M=2$ is attained. Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the
non-constant part is essentially rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$. The degenerate
case $a=b$ gives $M\equiv aJ$, ${\rm rk}M=1$, and $A$ or $B$ empty also
gives rank $1$.

The formal five-term writing $R=J-R_c+H+V-O$ collapses because
$R_c-H-V+O=(r-h)(c-v)^{T}=\rho\sigma^{T}$ is already rank one; $J,R_c,H,V,O$
are linearly dependent on the exact axis-aligned couped cross. The $3,4,5$
and unbounded ranks arise from replacing the cross by a non-rectangular
emblem e.g. a disc/shield whose $0\!-\!1$ indicator has rank growing with
resolution, or from treating the five rectangle indicators as independent
before cancellation. The current round consensus of colleagues 1-10 is
unanimous for the St George couped cross model: maximal rank $2$ for
$a\neq b$, essential rank $1$ for the white pattern, $1$ in the trivial
$a=b$ or degenerate pixelation case. Colleague 10’s earlier rank-5 claim
is now retracted as over-counting of non-independent rectangle indicators.
The rectangular shield idealisation gives the often quoted $1+2=3$ total
rank, $2$ non-constant, and the true geometric disc gives unbounded rank
in the infinite resolution limit, but those are different models from the
actual couped cross of the Tongan flag.
